newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova reviews tobacco tender, may bring in B.A.T..
newsitem.headline: Moldova reviews tobacco tender, may bring in B.A.T..

text.p: Moldova's new government plans to review the results of a tender seeking a foreign partner for its key tobacco industry, giving Britain's B.A.T. Industries plc a new chance to win the deal.
"We cancelled the results of the tender. We are looking for another option," Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc told reporters.
Officials at both Reemtsma Cigarettenfabriken GmbH, which won the tender, and its rival B.A.T., said their companies had not been formally notified that the tender had been cancelled.
This week B.A.T. executives met Moldova's new president, Petru Lucinschi, Ciubuc, and agriculture ministry officials to discuss setting up a joint venture.

"Our message was that we are still interested in investing in Moldova, we are able to move very quickly, and the government has to do something very quickly, if it wishes to save 1997 tobacco crop," a B.A.T. official said.
Lucinschi's press service said after the meeting that the president had promised "to do everything in his power to create certain possibilities for realizing the British businessmen's plans".

A tender committee set up by the previous government had selected Reemtsma, controlled by privately owned German food group Tchibo Holding AG, in May last year to set up a joint venture with tobacco producers, Moldova's second biggest industry after wine production.
Both Reemtsma and B.A.T. had submitted bids, for the venture in which the foreign partner would hold 60 percent.
But the joint venture documents have not yet been signed
Moldovan government sources said the government can start negotiations with the runner-up to the tender, according to the tender rules, so long as the documents for the venture are not signed.
Under the privatisation scheme, Moldova converted the industry, valued by international auditors Arthur Andersen at $35-65 million, into a joint-stock company called Tutun SA.
Tutun, which has initial capital of 205 million lei ($46 million), comprises a cigarette factory in Chisinau and eight fermentation plants.
In the original tender B.A.T. offered to invest $50 million in tobacco cultivation and cigarette production, while Reemtsma offered $59 million.
B.A.T. offered an additional $21 million of "soft investment" in the form of know-how and personnel training, while Reemtsma offered $10 million for this.
Parliament criticised the tender committee for awarding the deal to Reemtsma, and a final decision was postponed until after presidential elections in December and the formation of a new government.
Moldova, a small agricultural former Soviet republic lying between Ukraine and Romania, has been cultivating tobacco since 1840.

It used to account for one third of the Soviet Union's entire tobacco crop, harvesting up to 135,000 tons of tobacco leaves a year, exporting most of the crop and producing up to 10 billion cigarettes a year.
In 1996 Moldova harvested 19,000 tonnes of tobacco leaves and produced 9.7 billion cigarettes.
